Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Saadian army, led by Muhammad al-Harran, son of Muhammad al-Shaykh, conquered the city in June 1550, but the army was partly diverted to the Tafilalt soon after in order to suppress a rebellion there by the exiled Ahmad al-Araj.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-_____ was in turn preoccupied by other rebellions and was unable to send more reinforcements to his son
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Saadian army, led by Muhammad al-Harran, son of Muhammad al-Shaykh, conquered the city in June 1550, but the army was partly diverted to the Tafilalt soon after in order to suppress a rebellion there by the exiled Ahmad al-Araj. Al-Shaykh was in turn preoccupied by other rebellions and was unable to send more reinforcements to his son.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-Harran died of sickness in Tlemcen shortly before an army of Ottoman Janissaries and tribal allies sent by the Ottoman Pasha of Algiers, Hasan Pasha, expelled the Saadian forces from the city and f
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Al-Harran died of sickness in Tlemcen shortly before an army of Ottoman Janissaries and tribal allies sent by the Ottoman Pasha of Algiers, Hasan Pasha, expelled the Saadian forces from the city and from western Algeria in February 1551.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The Ottoman sultan, Suleiman the Magnificent, sent a diplomatic embassy to Muhammad al-Shaykh in _____ in an attempt to persuade the latter to accept Ottoman suzerainty, even if just nominally, but th
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Ottoman sultan, Suleiman the Magnificent, sent a diplomatic embassy to Muhammad al-Shaykh in 1552 in an attempt to persuade the latter to accept Ottoman suzerainty, even if just nominally, but this was refused.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The Ottomans sent an army, including Janissaries again, led by Salah Ra'is to attack Fes, where they defeated the Saadians in January _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Ottomans sent an army, including Janissaries again, led by Salah Ra'is to attack Fes, where they defeated the Saadians in January 1554.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: They installed '_____, an uncle of Ahmad al-Wattasi who had taken refuge in Spain, as ruler and Ottoman vassal in what was the final attempt by the Wattasids to regain power
Saadi Sultanate.fact: They installed 'Ali Abu Hassun, an uncle of Ahmad al-Wattasi who had taken refuge in Spain, as ruler and Ottoman vassal in what was the final attempt by the Wattasids to regain power.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Meanwhile, Ahmad al-Araj and his son Zaydan had made themselves lords of the _____, and allied themselves with Abu Hassun
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Meanwhile, Ahmad al-Araj and his son Zaydan had made themselves lords of the Tafilalt, and allied themselves with Abu Hassun. However, Muhammad al-Shaykh intercepted Abu Hassun's message to his potential allies in the Tafilalt that would have informed them of his victory in Fes.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: However, _____ al-Shaykh intercepted Abu Hassun's message to his potential allies in the Tafilalt that would have informed them of his victory in Fes
Saadi Sultanate.fact: However, Muhammad al-Shaykh intercepted Abu Hassun's message to his potential allies in the Tafilalt that would have informed them of his victory in Fes.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: As a result, Al-Araj and his son, believing that their side had lost, surrendered to Al-_____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: However, Muhammad al-Shaykh intercepted Abu Hassun's message to his potential allies in the Tafilalt that would have informed them of his victory in Fes. As a result, Al-Araj and his son, believing that their side had lost, surrendered to Al-Shaykh.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The latter went on to defeat Abu Hassun at the Battle of Tadla and to retake Fes in September _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The latter went on to defeat Abu Hassun at the Battle of Tadla and to retake Fes in September 1554.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Abu Hassun died in the battle, putting a definitive end to _____ prospects in Morocco
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Abu Hassun died in the battle, putting a definitive end to Wattasid prospects in Morocco.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Alcaudete concluded an agreement in _____ to offer Al-Shaykh Spanish troops, but the Spanish government initially refused to endorse the plan
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Alcaudete concluded an agreement in 1555 to offer Al-Shaykh Spanish troops, but the Spanish government initially refused to endorse the plan.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Meanwhile, Al-_____ had his older brother, Ahmad al-Araj, executed along with many of his sons and grandsons, thus securing the succession of his own son Abdallah
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Immediately after this, Muhammad al-Shaykh entered into negotiations with Count Alcaudete, the governor and general of the Spanish forces occupying Oran and other positions on the Algerian coast, to secure an anti-Ottoman alliance with Spain. Alcaudete concluded an agreement in 1555 to offer Al-Shaykh Spanish troops, but the Spanish government initially refused to endorse the plan.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Saadian forces also managed to occupy Tlemcen again in _____ while the Ottomans were preoccupied with besieging the Spanish in Oran
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Saadian forces also managed to occupy Tlemcen again in 1556 while the Ottomans were preoccupied with besieging the Spanish in Oran.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In the summer of _____ the Ottoman sultan sent another ambassador to Al-Shaykh demanding more forcefully that he accept Ottoman overlordship, which Al-Shaykh rejected with defiance and contempt
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In the summer of 1557 the Ottoman sultan sent another ambassador to Al-Shaykh demanding more forcefully that he accept Ottoman overlordship, which Al-Shaykh rejected with defiance and contempt.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: At the same time, three of his brothers – Abd al-Malik, Ahmad, and Abd al-Mu'min – fled the country in fear of assassination and took refuge with the _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Saadian forces also managed to occupy Tlemcen again in 1556 while the Ottomans were preoccupied with besieging the Spanish in Oran. At the same time, three of his brothers – Abd al-Malik, Ahmad, and Abd al-Mu'min – fled the country in fear of assassination and took refuge with the Ottomans.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Hasan Pasha, re-appointed as _____ pasha of Algiers, also sent an army to expel the Saadians from Tlemcen once again
Saadi Sultanate.fact: On October 23 of the same year, Muhammad al-Shaykh was assassinated – reportedly on the orders of the Ottoman sultan – by a Turkish member of his bodyguard, Salah ibn Kyahya, who had posed as an Ottoman deserter. At the same time, three of his brothers – Abd al-Malik, Ahmad, and Abd al-Mu'min – fled the country in fear of assassination and took refuge with the Ottomans.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The Saadians evacuated the city and were pursued by the Ottomans into Morocco, resulting in the Battle of Wadi al-Laban to the north of Fez in early _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Saadians evacuated the city and were pursued by the Ottomans into Morocco, resulting in the Battle of Wadi al-Laban to the north of Fez in early 1558.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Count Alcaudete, in turn, seeing that his alliance with _____ al-Shaykh was now moot, attempted to attack Mustaghanim in Algeria, where he died in a disastrous defeat for the Spanish
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Count Alcaudete, in turn, seeing that his alliance with Muhammad al-Shaykh was now moot, attempted to attack Mustaghanim in Algeria, where he died in a disastrous defeat for the Spanish.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In _____ or 1561 he launched another expedition to re-occupy Tlemcen which failed, marking the end of Saadian attempts to expand eastward
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In 1560 or 1561 he launched another expedition to re-occupy Tlemcen which failed, marking the end of Saadian attempts to expand eastward.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: To counter _____ and Spanish influence, Al-Ghalib sought to develop relations with France and Northern European powers
Saadi Sultanate.fact: To counter Ottoman and Spanish influence, Al-Ghalib sought to develop relations with France and Northern European powers. In the end, Ottoman pressure on Morocco was reduced by their own defeat at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He also supported the Morisco uprisings in Spain between _____ and 1570
Saadi Sultanate.fact: He also supported the Morisco uprisings in Spain between 1568 and 1570.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In the end, Ottoman pressure on Morocco was reduced by their own defeat at the Battle of Lepanto in _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In the end, Ottoman pressure on Morocco was reduced by their own defeat at the Battle of Lepanto in 1571.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Among other things, he built the Mouassine Mosque and the _____, redeveloped the royal palaces in the Kasbah, repaired the Kasbah Mosque, and started the Saadian Tombs
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Among other things, he built the Mouassine Mosque and the Ben Youssef Madrasa, redeveloped the royal palaces in the Kasbah, repaired the Kasbah Mosque, and started the Saadian Tombs.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Upon Abdallah al-Ghalib's death in _____ his son Muhammad II al-Mutawakkil inherited the throne
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Upon Abdallah al-Ghalib's death in 1574 his son Muhammad II al-Mutawakkil inherited the throne. He served in the Ottoman army and won some favour by participating in the successful Ottoman Siege of Tunis in 1574, which expelled the Spanish forces there.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He served in the Ottoman army and won some favour by participating in the successful Ottoman Siege of Tunis in _____, which expelled the Spanish forces there
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Upon Abdallah al-Ghalib's death in 1574 his son Muhammad II al-Mutawakkil inherited the throne. He served in the Ottoman army and won some favour by participating in the successful Ottoman Siege of Tunis in 1574, which expelled the Spanish forces there.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Meanwhile, his uncle, Abd al-Malik, had worked to further secure _____ support
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Meanwhile, his uncle, Abd al-Malik, had worked to further secure Ottoman support. He served in the Ottoman army and won some favour by participating in the successful Ottoman Siege of Tunis in 1574, which expelled the Spanish forces there.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: That same year he travelled to _____ and obtained support for his bid to the Saadian throne from the Ottoman sultan Murad III himself
Saadi Sultanate.fact: That same year he travelled to Istanbul and obtained support for his bid to the Saadian throne from the Ottoman sultan Murad III himself.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Soon afterwards the sultan ordered the beylerbey (governor) of Algiers, _____, to assist Abd al-Malik in invading Morocco
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Soon afterwards the sultan ordered the beylerbey (governor) of Algiers, Ramazan Pasha, to assist Abd al-Malik in invading Morocco.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In early 1576 the Ottoman army, including a contingent of Janissaries and a supplement of troops led by Abd al-Malik himself, won a decisive victory at the Battle of ar-Rukn near Fez, _____ik to depose Al-Mutawakkil, who fled
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In early 1576 the Ottoman army, including a contingent of Janissaries and a supplement of troops led by Abd al-Malik himself, won a decisive victory at the Battle of ar-Rukn near Fez, allowing Abd al-Malik to depose Al-Mutawakkil, who fled.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: This made him the first _____ ruler to accept vassal status with a foreign power
Saadi Sultanate.fact: This made him the first Saadian ruler to accept vassal status with a foreign power.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He also sent the majority of _____ troops who had helped him – including the Janissaries – back to Algiers shortly after winning his throne
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Once on the throne, as an Ottoman vassal, Abd al-Malik had the Friday prayers and the khutba in mosques delivered in the Ottoman sultan's name, adopted Ottoman clothing, and organized his army along Ottoman lines with the help of Turkish officers. Nonetheless, Abd al-Malik remained wary of Ottoman motives towards his kingdom and maintained relations with Spain as well as continuing to pursue relations with France (King Henri III) and England (Queen Elizabeth).

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Meanwhile, his deposed nephew, Al-_____, sought help from Portugal, whose king, Sebastian I, felt he had the most to lose from the increased Ottoman influence in the region
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Meanwhile, his deposed nephew, Al-Mutawakkil, sought help from Portugal, whose king, Sebastian I, felt he had the most to lose from the increased Ottoman influence in the region. Sebastian endorsed Al-Mutawakkil's claim and in July 1578 he crossed over into northern Morocco with an army, accompanied by the deposed sultan.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Sebastian endorsed Al-Mutawakkil's claim and in July _____ he crossed over into northern Morocco with an army, accompanied by the deposed sultan
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Sebastian endorsed Al-Mutawakkil's claim and in July 1578 he crossed over into northern Morocco with an army, accompanied by the deposed sultan.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Sebastian, however, did not use the fortified _____ positions along the coast to his advantage and instead decided to march directly into the country's interior
Saadi Sultanate.fact: While Moroccan sources exaggerate the size of his army, there was no doubt that it was impressive, with the Portuguese king promoting his campaign to the rest of Europe as a crusade and hiring a large force of mercenaries. Sebastian, however, did not use the fortified Portuguese positions along the coast to his advantage and instead decided to march directly into the country's interior.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The Saadian army, led by Abd al-Malik, accompanied by his brother Ahmad (yet another son of _____ al-Shaykh), met the Portuguese at Wadi al-Makhazin near Ksar al-Kebir on August 4
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Saadian army, led by Abd al-Malik, accompanied by his brother Ahmad (yet another son of Muhammad al-Shaykh), met the Portuguese at Wadi al-Makhazin near Ksar al-Kebir on August 4.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In the ensuing battle, known as the Battle of Wadi al-_____ or the Battle of Alcácer Quibir, the Saadians inflicted a heavy defeat on the Portuguese
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The Saadian army, led by Abd al-Malik, accompanied by his brother Ahmad (yet another son of Muhammad al-Shaykh), met the Portuguese at Wadi al-Makhazin near Ksar al-Kebir on August 4. In the ensuing battle, called the Battle of Wadi al-Makhazin or the Battle of Alcácer Quibir, the Saadians inflicted a heavy defeat on the Portuguese.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: As a result of the presence and death of these three, the _____ battle is also known as the "Battle of the Three Kings"
Saadi Sultanate.fact: As a result of the presence and death of these three, the 1578 battle is also called the "Battle of the Three Kings".

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The most immediate result was the accession of Abd al-Malik's brother Ahmad to the throne of _____
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Both King Sebastian and Al-Mutawakkil were killed in the battle, while on the Moroccan side Abd al-Malik also died during the battle in uncertain circumstances – either in combat or, by some accounts, poisoned by one of his Turkish officers in order to secure total Ottoman control of Morocco in the aftermath. The most immediate result was the accession of Abd al-Malik's brother Ahmad to the throne of Morocco.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Drawing on the prestige of the victory, he took on the regnal title (laqab) "al-_____"
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Drawing on the prestige of the victory, he took on the regnal title (laqab) "al-Mansur".

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The capture of a large number of _____ knights and nobility resulted in a flurry of ransoms which drained Portugal's finances while filling the coffers of the Saadian state
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The capture of a large number of Portuguese knights and nobility resulted in a flurry of ransoms which drained Portugal's finances while filling the coffers of the Saadian state.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: This allowed the sultan to strike new and higher-quality gold coins, earning him the additional title "ad-_____" ("the Golden")
Saadi Sultanate.fact: This allowed the sultan to strike new and higher-quality gold coins, earning him the additional title "ad-Dhahabi" ("the Golden").

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In the long term, _____'s international standing was greatly increased, giving it the status of a major regional power in the western Mediterranean
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In the long term, Morocco's international standing was greatly increased, giving it the status of a major regional power in the western Mediterranean.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The subsequent 24-year reign of Ahmad al-Mansur, among the longest in _____ history, marked the apogee of Saadian power and wealth
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The subsequent 24-year reign of Ahmad al-Mansur, among the longest in Moroccan history, marked the apogee of Saadian power and wealth. One consequence of this was a widespread adoption of firearms and artillery in the Moroccan military, which aided Al-Mansur in his later conquests.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: One consequence of this was a widespread adoption of firearms and artillery in the _____ military, which aided Al-Mansur in his later conquests
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The subsequent 24-year reign of Ahmad al-Mansur, among the longest in Moroccan history, marked the apogee of Saadian power and wealth. One consequence of this was a widespread adoption of firearms and artillery in the Moroccan military, which aided Al-Mansur in his later conquests.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In addition to local troops from the Sous and various tribes, the army also included troops from the _____ tribe, Andalusian recruits, and European mercenaries
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In addition to local troops from the Sous and various tribes, the army also included troops from the Algerian Zuwawa tribe, Andalusian recruits, and European mercenaries.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Possibly to limit _____/Ottoman influence, Al-Mansur entrusted the highest military positions to Andalusians and Europeans, and also employed them as his personal guard on campaigns
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Turkish titles and terms like beylerbey and sipahi were also used in the army. Possibly to limit Turkish/Ottoman influence, Al-Mansur entrusted the highest military positions to Andalusians and Europeans, and also employed them as his personal guard on campaigns.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-_____'s army, in turn, helped him ensure his absolute authority, turning the institution of government into a more dominant force across the country
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Possibly to limit Turkish/Ottoman influence, Al-Mansur entrusted the highest military positions to Andalusians and Europeans, and also employed them as his personal guard on campaigns. Al-Mansur's army, in turn, helped him ensure his absolute authority, turning the institution of government into a more dominant force across the country.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Nonetheless, the _____' status as sharifs, descendants of Muhammad, aided them in maintaining their legitimacy even in the face of this criticism
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Nonetheless, the Saadians' status as sharifs, descendants of Muhammad, aided them in maintaining their legitimacy even in the face of this criticism.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-_____ also insisted on maintaining a highly efficient state administration and remained personally involved in the state's affairs
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Al-Mansur also insisted on maintaining a highly efficient state administration and remained personally involved in the state's affairs.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He was a patron of culture, sponsoring poets, musicians, scholars, and elaborate ceremonies for religious festivals such as the Mawlid (birthday of the _____) and Eid al-Fitr
Saadi Sultanate.fact: He was a patron of culture, sponsoring poets, musicians, scholars, and elaborate ceremonies for religious festivals such as the Mawlid (birthday of the Prophet) and Eid al-Fitr.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In addition to the heavy taxation and the ransoms extorted from the _____ nobility, the wealth of al-Mansur's reign was also due to the Saadians' control of the sugar trade
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In addition to the heavy taxation and the ransoms extorted from the Portuguese nobility, the wealth of al-Mansur's reign was also due to the Saadians' control of the sugar trade.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Morocco was at that time a significant exporter of sugar towards _____, along with other products such as silk, copper, and leather
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Morocco was at that time a significant exporter of sugar towards Europe, along with other products such as silk, copper, and leather.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-_____ had ambivalent relations with the Ottoman Empire
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In addition to the heavy taxation and the ransoms extorted from the Portuguese nobility, the wealth of al-Mansur's reign was also due to the Saadians' control of the sugar trade. Al-Mansur had ambivalent relations with the Ottoman Empire.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: At the very start of his reign he formally recognized the suzerainty of the _____ sultan, as Abd al-Malik had done, while still remaining de facto independent
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Al-Mansur had ambivalent relations with the Ottoman Empire. At the very start of his reign he formally recognized the suzerainty of the Ottoman sultan, as Abd al-Malik had done, while still remaining de facto independent.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: However he quickly alienated the Ottoman sultan when he favorably received the Spanish embassy in _____, who brought him lavish gifts, and then reportedly trampled the symbol of Ottoman suzerainty bef
Saadi Sultanate.fact: However he quickly alienated the Ottoman sultan when he favorably received the Spanish embassy in 1579, who brought him lavish gifts, and then reportedly trampled the symbol of Ottoman suzerainty before a Spanish embassy in 1581.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He also suspected that the _____ were involved in the first rebellions against him in his early reign
Saadi Sultanate.fact: He also suspected that the Ottomans were involved in the first rebellions against him in his early reign.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: As a result, he minted coins in his own name and had Friday prayers delivered in his name instead of in the name of _____, the Ottoman sultan
Saadi Sultanate.fact: As a result, he minted coins in his own name and had Friday prayers delivered in his name instead of in the name of Murad III, the Ottoman sultan. In response to the removal of his name from Friday prayers, Murad III began preparations for an attack on Morocco.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He paid a tribute of over 100,000 gold coins, agreed to show respect to the _____ sultan and in return he was left alone
Saadi Sultanate.fact: As a result, he minted coins in his own name and had Friday prayers delivered in his name instead of in the name of Murad III, the Ottoman sultan. He paid a tribute of over 100,000 gold coins, agreed to show respect to the Ottoman sultan and in return he was left alone.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: In _____ Al-Mansur was also forced to agree to a special Ottoman "protection" over Morocco and to pay a certain tribute in order to stop the attacks from Algerian corsairs on the Moroccan coast and on
Saadi Sultanate.fact: In 1582 Al-Mansur was also forced to agree to a special Ottoman "protection" over Morocco and to pay a certain tribute in order to stop the attacks from Algerian corsairs on the Moroccan coast and on Moroccan ships.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-Mansur sent a payment to _____ every year, which the Saadians interpreted as a "gift" to the Ottomans while the Ottomans considered it a "tribute"
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The embassy nearly failed to reach Istanbul due to the opposition of Uluç (later called Kılıç Ali Paşa), the Ottoman Grand Admiral in Algiers who hoped to have Morocco invaded and incorporated into Ottoman Algeria's sphere of influence. Al-Mansur sent a payment to Istanbul every year, which the Saadians interpreted as a "gift" to the Ottomans while the Ottomans considered it a "tribute".

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Al-_____ would also pursue careful diplomatic relations with Europe
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Al-Mansur even felt confident enough after 1587 to drop his regular payments to Murad III. Al-Mansur would also pursue careful diplomatic relations with Europe.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: He was widely perceived as friendly to Spain, presumably seeing it as a counterweight to _____ influence and seeking to play the two against each other
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Despite the evident limits of his rule, he officially proclaimed himself caliph in the later part of his reign, seeing himself as the rival, rather than subordinate, of the Ottomans, and even as the rightful leader of the Muslim world. He was widely perceived as friendly to Spain, presumably seeing it as a counterweight to Ottoman influence and seeking to play the two against each other.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Nonetheless, he also sought alternatives to Spain by pursuing relations with the northern _____ states
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Nonetheless, he also sought alternatives to Spain by pursuing relations with the northern European states.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Most notably, he increased friendly relations with England when the latter made diplomatic overtures to him after _____ with a view to find allies against Spain at the time
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Most notably, he increased friendly relations with England when the latter made diplomatic overtures to him after 1580 with a view to find allies against Spain at the time.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: This led to the development of an Anglo-_____ alliance
Saadi Sultanate.fact: This led to the development of an Anglo-Moroccan alliance. This trade initially consisted of English cloth for Moroccan sugar, but after 1572 the English learned that they could find saltpeter and mainly sought to obtain this material.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: Early relations focused on trade as _____ merchants, despite the objections of the Portuguese, had been trading in Morocco since the early 16th century
Saadi Sultanate.fact: Early relations focused on trade as English merchants, despite the objections of the Portuguese, had been trading in Morocco since the early 16th century. This trade initially consisted of English cloth for Moroccan sugar, but after 1572 the English learned that they could find saltpeter and mainly sought to obtain this material.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: This trade initially consisted of English cloth for Moroccan sugar, but after _____ the English learned that they could find saltpeter and mainly sought to obtain this material
Saadi Sultanate.fact: This trade initially consisted of English cloth for Moroccan sugar, but after 1572 the English learned that they could find saltpeter and mainly sought to obtain this material.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: At that time, Sultan al-_____ demanded cannonballs in exchange, and from this time on the English were often supplying the Saadians with weapons and military equipment
Saadi Sultanate.fact: At that time, Sultan al-Mutawakkil demanded cannonballs in exchange, and from this time on the English were often supplying the Saadians with weapons and military equipment.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: However, after Spain's annexation of Portugal in _____ the Queen accorded more importance to securing cordial relations with the Saadian sultan and in 1581 she allowed English naval timber to be expor
Saadi Sultanate.fact: However, after Spain's annexation of Portugal in 1580 the Queen accorded more importance to securing cordial relations with the Saadian sultan and in 1581 she allowed English naval timber to be exported to Morocco in return for saltpeter.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: John Symcot, an agent of the Earl of Leicester, was able to obtain in _____ a royal charter to found the English Barbary Company, which managed the activities of English traders in Morocco and obtaine
Saadi Sultanate.fact: John Symcot, an agent of the Earl of Leicester, was able to obtain in 1585 a royal charter to found the English Barbary Company, which managed the activities of English traders in Morocco and obtained trading privileges from the sultan.

Saadi Sultanate.subject: Environment & Ecology
Saadi Sultanate.question: The English also attempted to convince Al-Mansur to support _____, the claimant to the Portuguese throne against the Spanish, but Al-Mansur was evasive in his responses
Saadi Sultanate.fact: The English also attempted to convince Al-Mansur to support Don Antonio, the claimant to the Portuguese throne against the Spanish, but Al-Mansur was evasive in his responses.
